items.title: Cale Makar agrees to eight-year extension with Avalanche
items.author: Chris Schommer
items.body: Cale Makar has agreed to an eight-year, $163.2 million contract extension with the Colorado Avalanche according to Elliotte Friedman.
items.impact: Maker’s extension makes the blueliner the highest-paid skater in NHL history

items.title: Macklin Celebrini agrees to five-year extension with Sharks
items.author: Chris Schommer
items.body: Macklin Celebrini has agreed to a five-year, $94 million contract extension with the San Jose Sharks according to Frank Seravalli.
items.impact: Celebrini’s extension will make him the highest paid player in the league after the center exploded for 115 points (45 goals, 70 assists) over 82 games in 2025-26. The dynamic third-year superstar is part of an exciting young forward core for a San Jose squad looking to reach the postseason this upcoming season.

items.title: Connor Bedard (shoulder) agrees to five-year extension with Blackhawks
items.author: Chris Schommer
items.body: Connor Bedard (shoulder) has agreed to a five-year, $75 million contract extension with the Chicago Blackhawks according to Charlie Roumeliotis.
items.impact: Bedard’s extension keeps the superstar center in Chicago through the 2030-31 season. The organization will likely be without there dynamic forward for at least the first month of the upcoming 2026-27 season after undergoing shoulder surgery July 8.

items.title: Anders Lee signs three-year deal with Mammoth
items.author: Chris Schommer
items.body: Anders Lee has agreed to a three-year, $16.2 million deal with the Utah Mammoth according to Elliotte Friedman.
items.impact: Lee cashed in on the open market after spending his entire career with the New York Islanders, providing another impactful veteran forward option on an Utah squad looking to reach the postseason this upcoming season. The veteran winger posted 42 points (19 goals, 23 assists) over 82 contests in 2025-26 and remains a reliable two-way forward option this upcoming season.

items.title: Alex Ovechkin agrees to one-year deal with Capitals
items.author: Chris Schommer
items.body: Alex Ovechkin has agreed to a one-year, $4.25 million contract to return to the Washington Capitals.
items.impact: Ovechkin’s deal includes a $4.75 million incentive if the superstar winger suits up for at least 10 games during the 2026-27 season. The veteran saw enough investment from the front office with the acquisitions of Alex Tuch and Jordan Kyrou to return to chase another Stanley Cup after posting 64 points (32 goals, 32 assists) over 82 contests in 2025-25 for head coach Spencer Carberry.

items.title: Frederik Andersen signs with Oilers
items.author: Chris Schommer

items.title: Sergei Bobrovsky agrees to deal with Maple Leafs
items.author: Chris Schommer
items.body: Sergei Bobrovsky has agreed to a three-year, $21 million contract with the Toronto Maple Leafs.
items.impact: Bobrovsky became a top target to begin free agency for the Maple Leafs after the Florida Panthers traded for netminder Jacob Markstrom, solidifying a shaky position for a club looking to return to the postseason after a disappointing 2025-26 campaign. The veteran posted a less than desirable .877 save percentage and 3.07 GAA with four shutouts over 51 starts (27-23-1) for the Panthers last season, but will look to bounce back as an elite netminding option for fantasy managers this upcoming season.

items.title: Brady Tkachuk dealt to Panthers
items.author: Chris Schommer
items.body: The Ottawa Senators have agreed to trade Brady Tkachuk to the Florida Panthers according to Elliotte Friedman.
items.impact: Tkachuk will reunite with brother Matthew with the Panthers, with Ottawa receiving the #9 and #25 picks in the first round of the upcoming NHL draft as well as a first-round pick in 2029 and a second-round pick in 2030. The gritty winger joins a Florida squad looking to bounce back from a disappointing campaign plagued by injuries to key players in hopes of another Stanley Cup run in 2026-27.
